Hi Mina / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the demo last week — excited to move forward. Attaching our redlines for the MSA and DPA and a short data-residency matrix. Two asks up front:

1) We are asking for a carveout to the data residency clause for EU-sourced PII when processed by third-party analytics vendors. We can provide a list of subprocessors; we need a POA to keep EU data in-region where required.

2) Liability cap: our investors require a $3M aggregate cap for this class of integration; Redwood's standard is higher. Can we discuss a tiered cap tied to annual committed spend?

I've attached OrchidEdge_MSA_redline_v3.docx and orchidedge_dpa_proposed.pdf — the DPA has proposed subprocessor language we'd like Redwood to accept.

Next steps: can your legal/procurement team confirm what is negotiable vs. not? We're aiming to sign SOW and start integration work the week of July 12.

Thanks,
Suresh

Subject: RE: OrchidEdge redlines (MSA/DPA/SOW) — triage notes

Mina — triage below (high level). I've attached an internal cheatsheet (MSA_redline_cheatsheet.md) mapping each clause to negotiation posture and fallback language.

Top issues we need to resolve before committing to SOW start date:

- Liability cap: Orchidedge asks for $3M aggregate. Redwood standard is $10M / 3x annual fees for strategic partners. Proposal: Tiered approach:
  * Option A (preferred): For first 12 months post-signing, cap = $3M. After first year, cap reverts to standard $10M unless annual committed spend >= $1.2M, in which case we keep $10M. This limits early-stage exposure but preserves our enterprise posture.
  * Option B (procurement compromise): Cap = min($3M, 3x annual recurring fees) for 12 months, then renegotiate at renewal.

- Data residency / subprocessor: Orchidedge wants EU PII to remain in-region when processed by their analytics subprocessors. Our position:
  * We can accept region-based processing commitments in the SOW for customer-specific data flows (i.e., OrchidEdge account-level setting).
  * We cannot guarantee third-party subprocessors beyond our control, but will require OrchidEdge to provide an approved subprocessor list and agree to contractual commitments to keep EU PII in-region. If Orchidedge insists Redwood certify third-party subprocessors, that's a major escalation and needs legal sign-off.

- Audit & access logs: Orchidedge requests quarterly audit rights for EU regulatory customers. We can offer on-site / remote audit windows for specific controls but will require scope limits and a cost-recovery provision.

- SLA & remedies: Orchidedge added service credit language tied to 99.9% uptime. We can accept 99.9% for dedicated capacity; hosted plans are best‑effort with 99.5% financial SLA only for Dedicated. Need to mark SOW whether Orchidedge is going Dedicated or hosted.

Next steps for us: Ben — can you draft Option A liability language and a short paragraph for the SOW stating regional processing commitments (account-scoped) plus a subprocessor reporting cadence?

Kimberly
Director, Procurement Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: OrchardEdge MSA/DPA — proposed compromise language (Options A/B)

Suresh — attaching our redline with two negotiated options for the liability cap and a clean paragraph for regional processing. High-level summary below; full language is in OrchidEdge_MSA_redline_v3.docx (we've added tracked changes).

Key proposals (pick one):

Option A (recommended):
- Liability cap: For the first twelve (12) months following Effective Date, the aggregate liability cap for either party shall be $3,000,000. Thereafter, the cap shall be adjusted to the greater of (i) $10,000,000 or (ii) three (3) times the annual fees paid by OrchidEdge under this Agreement during the preceding 12-month period.

Option B (alternative):
- Liability cap: The aggregate liability cap shall be the lesser of $3,000,000 or three (3) times the annual fees paid by OrchidEdge, with both parties agreeing to good-faith renegotiation at each renewal.

Regional processing paragraph (SOW-level enforcement):
- Redwood will restrict processing of EU-designated personal data to data centers located within the EU for the services and features identified in the SOW. OrchidEdge shall provide Redwood with a list of approved subprocessors and agree to ensure any OrchidEdge-managed subprocessors maintain EU residency for EU-designated data. Redwood will provide a monthly subprocessor report; OrchidEdge may request (1) remediation or (2) removal from the subprocessor list subject to mutual agreement.

Audit & cost recovery: On-site or remote audits may be conducted with at least 30 days' notice; Redwood may invoice reasonable on-site audit costs.

SLA note: If OrchidEdge elects Dedicated capacity in the SOW, Redwood will commit to a 99.9% Uptime SLA with service credit remedies; Hosted plans remain 99.5% financial SLA.

Please confirm which liability option you prefer and whether OrchidEdge intends to include Dedicated capacity in the SOW. If you approve Option A, we can issue a DocuSign packet for signature (MSA + DPA + SOW).

Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
